takeaway: Tropical Wave #47 has moved off into the Pacific — Sunday is a quieter Pacífico Norte day with isolated afternoon showers, not yesterday’s widespread storms. Surf winds: Pacific onshore/side-on today (choppier after mid-morning); Caribbean easterlies rebuild Mon night through midweek for cleaner night/morning glass. Distant East Pacific activity stays along southern Mexico and farther west. Prolonged multi-day rain is now a watch-only, not an elevated weekend threat.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sun–Tue)
periods.pattern: Sunday mornings stay mostly clear to partly cloudy over Pacífico Norte, then isolated afternoon showers over the peninsula and mountains as leftover wave moisture mixes with sea breezes and daytime heat. Hot inland (Nicoya around 34°C, Liberia near 35°C). Monday–Tuesday look closer to typical rainy-season afternoons — more isolated than Saturday’s wave day. Official weekly guidance already called for a slight easing of Pacific rains early this week.
periods.implications: Best outdoor window is Sunday morning before isolated storms. For surf, expect choppier faces after mid-morning today; look for cleaner overnight/early sessions by Monday night into Tuesday if the northerly/easterly turn holds.
periods.confidence: High that Sunday is quieter than Saturday and no nearby cyclone hits Costa Rica. Moderate on exact Nosara shower timing and how clean Tuesday morning gets.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Wed–Sat)
periods.pattern: Ensemble averages keep Nicoya rain mostly light-to-moderate daily totals, not a stuck rain machine. Low-level flow favors Caribbean easterlies/northeast trades across Nicaragua and Nicoya much of midweek — clearer offshore quality than the weekend. Papagayo seas stay about 3–6 ft with north/northwest winds Tue–Wed; Thursday looks a bit more mixed with west/northwest elsewhere. Official longer outlook still leans drier than normal for Pacífico Norte into early October.
periods.implications: Better surf-wind stretch than the weekend: night/morning glass more reliable Wed–Fri. Nicaragua all-day offshore midweek is a good Nosara quality signal, but it does not mean Nosara stays glassy all day. Keep late-day plans flexible for quick storms.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the trade return and quieter theme; low–moderate for any midweek wetter spike if Pacific moisture reconnects, or if Thursday’s softer marine winds verify.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s longer-range outlook still leans drier than normal for the northern Pacific from late September into mid-October, with no official extreme-rain event flagged. Ensemble means show some moist days possible into early October, but without a Costa Rica–centered rain machine. Distant East Pacific activity remains focused near Mexico and farther west.
periods.implications: No prolonged flood-season spell is the baseline for Nicoya Pacific. Treat any wet day as a short cell unless a new watch develops.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the quieter-than-peak theme; low for day-by-day detail past about a week.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Residual concern mainly Sunday–Monday (27–28 Sep) while leftover wave moisture and Pacific flow overlap; baseline after that is quieter unless a Mexico-side system feeds moisture south
gyreWatch.supporting: Wave #47 spent Saturday over the country and left some leftover instability for Sunday. Broad moist Pacific flow remains nearby. Tropical Depression Eighteen-E (former Tehuantepec disturbance) sits a few hundred miles southwest of southern Mexico and could keep the far-Pacific moisture field active.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No closed gyre sits over Costa Rica or Nicaragua on the main ensemble averages. Official Sunday Pacífico Norte forecast is only isolated afternoon showers. Wave #47 is exiting west into the Pacific and ending its direct influence. Eighteen-E and the named storms track west-northwest along or well off Mexico, not toward Costa Rica. Midweek easterly trades argue against a stuck onshore rain machine. The longer official outlook still leans drier for northern Pacific into October.

surfWinds.regime: Pacific onshore Sunday → Caribbean easterlies / N–NW rebuilding Mon night–midweek
surfWinds.detail: Papagayo and near-coast models favor southwest/Pacific flow today — onshore/side-on for west-facing Nosara, so choppier faces after the morning lull. Overnight Sunday into Monday the marine forecast shifts toward north/northwest, then more solid NW–N midweek as Caribbean easterlies rebuild across Nicaragua and Nicoya. That is the classic offshore setup. Nicaragua all-day offshore midweek is a good Nosara quality signal, but it does not mean Nosara stays glassy all day. Thursday looks softer/more mixed (west–northwest elsewhere). Do not read Papagayo light/variable as all-day glass.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Early morning Sunday before the sea breeze. Cleaner overnight/morning glass Mon night through Fri if trades hold. No clean all-day offshore Sunday signal.
surfWinds.confidence: High on Sunday daytime onshore; moderate on how firmly trades lock Tue–Wed (some ensembles still show a light Pacific component early week).

whatChanged: Wave #47 is exiting into the Pacific (yesterday it was over the country). Saturday’s storm notice updates are aging — latest was Sat 4:50 p.m.; Sunday’s official Pacífico Norte call is only isolated afternoon showers. The Tehuantepec disturbance has become Tropical Depression Eighteen-E and still tracks west-northwest along southern Mexico, not toward Costa Rica. Polo, Odalys, and Nolo remain well west. Surf-wind improvement after Sunday night still looks on track. Prolonged-rain watch steps down from elevated to watch-only — no closed gyre on ensemble means.
practical: Best outdoors: Sunday morning before isolated afternoon storms; heat inland continues. For surf, prioritize early morning today; look for cleaner easterly/N–NW glass from about Monday night through midweek. Prolonged multi-day rain is not the baseline. Latest official storm notice: Saturday 4:50 p.m. covering Wave #47 as it exits.
